Stock Preachers News Commentary

VANCOUVER, BC, Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stocks skidded midweek as the Nasdaq Composite dropped 449 points, or 1.65%, to 26,755.24, pulling its weekly loss to 2.23%. The S&P 500 fell 1.10% on the day and 1.18% for the week, while the Russell 2000 tumbled 1.70% and now carries an RSI of just 28.3, signaling deeply oversold small caps. The Dow held up relatively better, down 0.29%. Gold slid 1.93%, silver dropped 5.81%, and WTI crude bucked the trend, rising 1.36% to $95.42 a barrel. Active Companies from around the markets with current developments this week include: RTX (NYSE: RTX), Lockheed Martin (NYSE: LMT), Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY), Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc. (TSX: ATD), and IBM (NYSE: IBM).

Stock Preachers Logo

The broad equity retreat left every major index in the red for the week, with the Nasdaq's 2.23% weekly slide the steepest among the four. The S&P 500 sits just above its 50-day simple moving average support of 7,707.03, while the Dow trades right around its 20-day SMA support near 51,489.97, leaving both indices on the edge of short-term technical floors.

Volatility ticked higher but remained contained, with the VIX up 0.95 points to 16.22 and the VXN rising to 21.14. Both gauges stayed within their recent weekly ranges, suggesting the selloff has not yet triggered panic-level hedging even as the Russell 2000's RSI of 28.3 points to small-cap stress running well ahead of the broader market's unease.

Commodities sent a mixed signal. WTI crude's 1.36% daily gain and 66.18% year-to-date advance stood in sharp contrast to gold's 1.93% drop and silver's 5.81% slide, the latter now down 20.54% year to date. The 10-year Treasury yield edged up 3 basis points to 5.25%, while the euro slipped 0.33% against the dollar.

The full report lays out the index-by-index support and resistance ladder, sector standouts, and what traders are watching into the back half of the week.

The markets are certainly in a see-saw this week, you can read more news on these companies and other sectors at: https://stockpreachers.com/articles/energy-and-pharma-hold-the-fort-as-tech-takes-it-on-the-chin/

In other industry developments and happenings in the market this week include:

RTX (NYSE: RTX) Raytheon, an RTX business, has secured a five-year contract with two additional option years, valued up to $6.3 billion, for the production and sustainment of Standard Missile-3 Block IB interceptors. The award is part of recent agreements between Raytheon and the Department of War supporting replenishment of missile defense inventory used in combat.

title: IBM: Is Customer Financing Flattering Its Cash Recovery?
detail:
IBM: Is Customer Financing Flattering Its Cash Recovery?
Jeff Lewis
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 9:13 AM CDT 4 min read
IBM
Trade IBM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

International Business Machines Corporation (NYSE:IBM) generated $7.77 billion of first-half 2026 operating cash flow, up from $6.07 billion a year earlier. Almost all the improvement came from financing-receivable movements. That matters as customers redirect technology budgets toward servers and memory: collecting existing balances strengthens liquidity, while sustainable cash growth still depends on profitable software, consulting and infrastructure sales. IBM is also positioning itself in next-generation computing, making it worth exploring these 10 Best Quantum Computing Stocks to Buy and Hold Forever.

International Business Machines Corporation (NYSE:IBM) carries a quoted forward P/E of 17x, against 21x trailing earnings. Reported and adjusted profits tell different stories. Acquisition amortization and certain retirement costs reduce reported earnings, while a substantial 2025 tax benefit lifted them. Those accounting effects make the cash performance behind expected earnings especially important. The valuation looks reasonable if operating improvement delivers management's annual cash-growth target. Read about IBM's valuation here.

Analysts expect calendar-2026 adjusted EPS growth of about 6% for International Business Machines Corporation (NYSE:IBM), versus 16% for SAP SE (NYSE:SAP), using each company's currency and adjustments. The software peer is the closer operating comparison for the growth thesis; Accenture plc (NYSE:ACN) benchmarks consulting. Its reported earnings follow U.S. GAAP, while SAP SE (NYSE:SAP) reports under IFRS.

JPMorgan Upgrades IBM on Stronger Software Growth Expectations
Receivables Explain the Cash Increase

For International Business Machines Corporation (NYSE:IBM), financing-receivable movements contributed $2.26 billion to first-half operating cash flow, compared with $606 million a year earlier. The $1.66 billion difference explains approximately 98% of the operating-cash-flow increase, by calculation. Releasing capital from customer financing produces real cash, but it can occur without stronger recurring profits.

International Business Machines Corporation (NYSE:IBM) defines non-GAAP free cash flow as operating cash flow excluding financing-receivable movements, less net capital expenditure. That measure was $4.76 billion, compared with $4.81 billion. The adjustment reveals a business whose first-half cash generation after investment was essentially unchanged.

Financing can support customer purchases and strengthen relationships. However, payment flexibility earns its return through collections and credit quality. Replacing collected balances with new financing can absorb cash again, making a repeatable earnings contribution more valuable than a temporary release of capital.

title: What Was HPE Telling You Before Its Stock Ran?
detail:
What Was HPE Telling You Before Its Stock Ran?
Trefis Team
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 10:12 AM CDT 4 min read
HPE
DELL
IBM
CSCO
SMCI
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) stock returned 187.1%, counting dividends, in the twelve months to October 13, 2026. On September 2, 2026, the company reported record quarterly revenue, orders, and backlog. Executives credited demand for traditional servers, AI systems and networking, along with higher prices for those servers. Did the company say anything about that demand, or those server prices, before October 2025?

HPE Praised AI Demand, Then Faulted Its Own Pricing

Executives addressed these trends twice, though only one instance sounded like good news at the time. During the December 5, 2024 call for fiscal Q4 2024, management noted that demand for AI systems remained strong. Revenue for that quarter reached a record $8.5 billion, up 15.1% from a year earlier.

Three months later, during the March 6, 2025 call for fiscal Q1 2025, executives identified servers as a problem. Management stated that HPE had priced its traditional servers without fully accounting for the value of its inventory, and that unusually high AI inventory had squeezed server margins further. Server operating margin stood at 8.1%, a figure management called well below expectations. The shares struggled after that report. Only in hindsight does this look like a sign, because server pricing is exactly what management would highlight eighteen months later.

Financial filings from HPE showed this same mix of rising sales and weaker margins. Revenue grew 18.5% from a year earlier in fiscal Q3 2025. Yet operating margin for that quarter fell to 4.7%, down from 7.8% a year earlier. The stock was already rising as well: it returned 74.7% in the six months before the twelve-month window began on October 10, 2025.

How Big Was HPE's Run Against The S&P 500?

The S&P 500 returned about 18% over the same twelve months. That means HPE returned roughly ten times as much as the broader index. Almost all of that gain materialized in the last six months, when the stock returned 183%. HPE was not alone in this trend: Dell Technologies, one of its peers, did even better at 285.0%. Not every peer joined in, though, as IBM fell 14.8%.

The shift linking back to those earlier earnings calls occurred in servers, HPE's largest business at 52% of fiscal 2025 revenue. Server revenue rose 35% to an all-time high in fiscal Q3 2026. Executives noted that higher average selling prices for traditional servers made up for supply limits on how many units HPE could ship. This trajectory looks like the March 2025 pricing problem reversed.

The market expects IBM (IBM) to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook is important in assessing the company's earnings picture, but a powerful factor that might influence its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The earnings report, which is expected to be released on October 21, might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This technology and consulting company is expected to post quarterly earnings of $2.87 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +8.3%.

Revenues are expected to be $16.84 billion, up 3.1% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.5% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts may not always get reflected in the aggregate change.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for IBM
Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

Accenture plc ACN offers investors a clear trade-off. Enterprise AI demand, recurring services and cash generation support the growth case, while uneven discretionary spending, pricing pressure and a heavier acquisition program raise execution risk.

The valuation is lower than several key benchmarks, but fiscal 2026 organic growth was about 3%. The question is whether AI-led demand can lift underlying growth enough to justify a more aggressive stance.

Accenture's Valuation Looks Discounted to Key Benchmarks

ACN trades at 14.4X forward 12-month earnings, below the Zacks sub-industry at 18.6X, the broader Zacks sector at 20.7X and the S&P 500 at 19.8X. The gap gives investors a valuation cushion if operating momentum improves.

The stock also trades well below its five-year median of 24.3X. That discount is meaningful, but valuation alone does not resolve concerns around organic growth, pricing and the contribution required from acquisitions.

ACN's AI Growth Supports the Bull Case

More than 400 clients initiated advanced AI work with Accenture in fiscal 2026, including nearly 100 in the fourth quarter. The company ended the year with nearly 110,000 AI and data professionals. Bookings from eight emerging AI and data partners more than tripled from fiscal 2025, while related revenues more than doubled.

International Business Machines Corporation IBM is also pushing enterprise AI deeper into consulting through large-scale deployment and modernization work. Cognizant Technology Solutions Corporation CTSH is expanding enterprise AI services around agentic systems and major cloud platforms. Their activity reinforces the competitive race to turn AI spending into consulting and managed-services revenue.

Accenture's M&A Push Raises Execution Costs

Accenture deployed $4.9 billion across 17 acquisitions in fiscal 2026. For fiscal 2027, it expects about $8 billion of acquisition investment, including roughly $3 billion tied to Cyber OT transactions that shifted into the new fiscal year and approximately $5 billion of additional planned investment.

The financing burden is rising with that strategy. A $5 billion bond offering completed in July 2026 is expected to add roughly $250 million of interest expense in fiscal 2027, while lower average cash balances are expected to reduce interest income by about $100 million. Successful integration and stronger organic growth therefore matter more.

Factors Shaping Upcoming Results

During the third quarter, IBM entered into a multi-year, $240 million agreement with Together AI to support the growing demand for enterprise artificial intelligence (AI) inference. The partnership will enable IBM to expand its cloud infrastructure offerings for open-source AI workloads and strengthen its position in the rapidly growing AI infrastructure market. IBM also introduced a new set of AI-powered experiences for the 2026 U.S. Open to make live tennis more personalized, informative and interactive for millions of fans worldwide. By turning complex court-level data into accessible insights, the company helped fans better understand the game through advanced technology. Such investments in innovation and collaborations will likely boost IBM's commercial prospects and are likely to have generated incremental revenues for the Software segment.

During the to-be-reported quarter, IBM partnered with India-based AI company Sarvam to develop and test sovereign AI technologies for government agencies and regulated industries in the subcontinent. The collaboration aims to build AI systems that give organizations greater control over data, governance and operations while supporting digital transformation across the public sector. IBM also collaborated with Arm Holdings plc ARM to give enterprises more software choices for mission-critical workloads. IBM's latest processor will enable Arm-native Linux environments to run alongside z/OS and Linux on IBM Z, giving enterprises access to a broader software ecosystem while maintaining security, reliability and scalability. These are likely to have generated additional revenues for the Consulting segment.

However, despite solid hybrid cloud, quantum technology and AI traction, IBM faces stiff competition from Amazon Web Services and Microsoft's Azure. The company is also facing challenges from AI firm Anthropic as the latter's Claude Code tool can modernize legacy COBOL systems — a foundational programming language deeply embedded in IBM's mainframe ecosystem. By proposing to substantially automate code exploration, documentation, refactoring and security analysis, Claude Code threatens to reduce enterprises' reliance on specialized legacy service providers like IBM, putting its business model at stake. This is likely to redefine the competitive landscape, leading to a broad-based downslide across the sector. Increasing pricing pressure is eroding margins, and profitability has trended down over the years, barring occasional spikes.

Accenture plc ACN has moved higher recently, shifting attention to whether improving business momentum can sustain the advance. Fiscal 2026 revenue growth, stronger fourth-quarter activity and rising enterprise AI adoption support the case for continued demand.

The counterweight is that acquisitions will supply a meaningful share of fiscal 2027 growth while discretionary spending, pricing and financing costs remain pressure points. That mix argues for a measured view of the rally.

Accenture's Rally Meets a Stronger Growth Narrative

Fiscal 2026 revenues reached $74.18 billion, increasing 5% in local currency. Growth strengthened in the fourth quarter, when revenues rose 7% in local currency and exceeded the company's guidance range.

For fiscal 2027, management expects 3%-6% local-currency revenue growth. Acquisitions are expected to contribute 2%-2.5%, leaving organic growth dependent on client spending and execution across consulting and managed services.

ACN's AI Momentum Adds Fuel to the Growth Case

More than 400 clients initiated advanced AI projects with Accenture in fiscal 2026, including nearly 100 in the fourth quarter. Bookings from eight emerging AI and data partners more than tripled from fiscal 2025, while related revenues more than doubled.

International Business Machines IBM is also expanding enterprise AI through its consulting business, including new services and partnerships aimed at deploying AI across business workflows. Cognizant Technology Solutions CTSH likewise continues to build enterprise AI capabilities, underscoring the competitive intensity around AI-led transformation services.

Managed Services Give Accenture Revenue Visibility

Managed Services generated $37.30 billion in fiscal 2026 revenues, up from $34.57 billion a year earlier and increasing 6% in local currency. The business grew faster than Consulting, which posted 3% local-currency growth for the year.

Fourth-quarter Managed Services bookings reached a record $12.77 billion, producing a 1.4 book-to-bill ratio. Full-year bookings were $43.67 billion, supporting visibility from multiyear and recurring client engagements.

ACN's Valuation Leaves Room but Risks Remain

ACN trades at 14.4X forward 12-month earnings, below the Zacks sub-industry's 18.6X and its own five-year median of 24.3X. That discount leaves room for a rerating if growth and execution improve.
